TENANT VOICE NS

PROJECT STATUS

- Active Development
- Current Phase: Spring 12 - Supabase Integration

MISSION

Tenant Voice NS exists to answer:

"What's it actually like to live there?"

Most rental platforms focus on:

- Advertisements
- Photos
- Landlord marketing

Tenant Voice NS focuses on:

- Tenant experiences
- Structured review data
- Property management quality
- Long-term renter insight

Core philosophy:

Reliable Rental Intelligence

--------------------------------------------------

PRODUCT PRINCIPLES

Property First

Users generally search for properties, not landlords.

Example:

Search:
Quest Towers

Not:
Quest Property Management

The application should always prioritize property discovery.

Reduce User Friction

Use:

- Autocomplete
- Dropdowns
- Predefined ranges

Avoid:

- Users typing identifiers
- Exact dates
- Free-form relationships

Trustworthy Data Over Maximum Data

If users don't know the answer:

Allow N/A

Bad data is worse than missing data.

--------------------------------------------------

CORE DATA MODEL

Landlord
↓
Property
↓
Review
↓
Property Ratings
Landlord Ratings

--------------------------------------------------

ENTITIES

LANDLORD

Represents:

- Property management companies
- Private landlords

Fields:

- id
- slug
- name
- type

PROPERTY

Primary object users search for.

Fields:

- id
- slug
- name
- address
- city
- landlord_id

REVIEW

Represents a tenant experience.

Fields:

- id
- property_id
- review_text
- occupancy_duration
- would_live_again
- created_at

--------------------------------------------------

CURRENT NEXT STEP

Spring 12 Floor 4

Connect:

Next.js
↓
Supabase

Tasks:

- Install Supabase client
- Configure .env.local
- Create Supabase client
- Query properties table
- Display results in app

--------------------------------------------------

FINAL PHILOSOPHY

Do not ask users for information they do not naturally know.

Examples:

- Property autocomplete
- Occupancy duration ranges
- N/A ratings
- Property-first search
- Structured scoring

Goal:

Collect reliable rental intelligence with the least possible user friction.

--------------------------------------------------

PLANNED UX BACKLOG

1. Working back navigation with preserved search state

- Replace placeholder "Back to ..." controls with working navigation.
- Preserve the Discover search term, results, and scroll position when returning from a property page.
- Support direct visits to a property page with a sensible fallback to Discover.
- Verify the search-to-property-to-back flow on mobile.

2. Functional navigation on every page

- Show the shared navigation at the top of every page and use real links rather than inactive buttons.
- Link Discover to `/` and Review to `/submit-review`.
- Property detail pages use `/properties/[slug]`.
- Decide what the Profiles navigation item should open. There is no generic Profiles page yet; landlord profiles are on the future roadmap. Do not leave this item pointing to a missing route.
- Check all navigation destinations and active states across the app.

3. Read-only star rating meters

- Show read-only star meters alongside the property and landlord summary scores near the top of each property page.
- Add read-only star meters for the property and landlord category ratings on each individual review card.
- Keep property ratings and landlord ratings visually distinct.
- Calculate summary scores from approved reviews: average numeric category scores within each review, then average those review scores; exclude N/A and reviews with no numeric ratings.
- Show the contributing review count and use "Not rated yet" when no numeric ratings are available.
- Display N/A as text, never as a zero-star score.
